audits.title: An audit to assess whether patients under the care of a community mental health team who are taking clozapine are having their lipid profile checked annually and are given lifestyle advice and have had a QRISK3 assessment
audits.standard: NICE: lipids at baseline, 3 months after starting a new antipsychotic, then annually; lifestyle advice and QRISK3 assessment

cycle1.result: 36 of 39 (92%) had lipids checked in last 12 months; 21 of 39 (54%) had cholesterol over 5.0; 9 of 39 (23%) had documented lifestyle discussion; 0 of 39 (0%) had QRISK3 assessment.

audits.intervention: Planned presentation to the CMHT and teaching on lifestyle advice and QRISK3.
audits.other_findings: 17 of 56 clozapine patients were excluded as already on cholesterol-lowering medication.
audits.citation: Linley-Adams E, Harris B. An audit to assess whether patients under the care of a community mental health team who are taking clozapine are having their lipid profile checked annually and are given lifestyle advice and have had a QRISK3 assessment. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S89-S89. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.272.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Clozapine Prescribing Practice and Monitoring Process in an Australian Community Mental Health Service
audits.standard: Monash Health clozapine patient management guidelines and RANZCP clinical practice guidelines

cycle1.result: Monthly weight, physical examination, medical officer review and full blood examination 97%; BMI monitoring 66.7%; six-monthly consultant review 42.4%; lipid profile 90.1%; echocardiogram 75.8%; most metabolic bloods 70–90%; all doses within recommended range.

audits.other_findings: Clozapine level was subtherapeutic in 54.5% and 54.5% were on an adjunct psychotropic. Hypersalivation (57.6%) and weight gain (39.4%) were the commonest side effects.
audits.citation: Fernando T, Bhandarkar R, Meadows G. Clinical Audit of Clozapine Prescribing Practice and Monitoring Process in an Australian Community Mental Health Service. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S4-S5. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.83.

audits.title: Audit of Physical Health Monitoring in Long-Stay Psychiatric Inpatients on Clozapine in NHS Ayrshire & Arran
audits.standard: Scottish Government 2017 National Standard for Monitoring the Physical Health of People Being Treated with Clozapine
audits.setting: Inpatient forensic and rehabilitation psychiatry services, NHS Ayrshire & Arran

cycle1.result: Fasting glucose in 10/18 and lipid profile in 12/18 in preceding 6 months; LFTs in 18/18 in last year; BMI, heart rate and blood pressure documented in all; ECG in 12/18 in last year.

audits.intervention: Physical health monitoring checklist planned for forensic wards.
audits.other_findings: The rehabilitation ward, which already used a monitoring checklist, achieved 100% adherence. Re-audit was planned in 6 months.
audits.citation: Carson C. Audit of Physical Health Monitoring in Long-Stay Psychiatric Inpatients on Clozapine in NHS Ayrshire & Arran. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S152-S152. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.409.

audits.title: Lipid Profile and Cardiovascular Risk Monitoring in Patients on Clozapine – an Audit at a Community Mental Health Resource Centre in Scotland
audits.standard: NICE guidance: lipid profile at baseline, 3 months and annually, and cardiovascular risk assessment with a validated tool (QRISK3 or ASSIGN score)
audits.setting: Community mental health resource centre (local CMHT)

cycle1.result: Lipid profile done in the past 12 months in 22/27 (81.1%); cardiovascular risk assessed in 1/27 (3.70%); lipid results communicated to GP in 4/22 (18.18%).

audits.intervention: Proposed structured process: clozapine clinic nurse creates an electronic task for the medic to review results, calculate cardiovascular risk and communicate lipids and risk to the GP in the annual review letter. Re-audit planned after 12 months.
audits.other_findings: Of 40 patients on clozapine, 13 were excluded (on statins, recently started, or outside age 30–74). Of those tested, 13/22 (59.9%) had total cholesterol above 5 mmol/L.
audits.citation: Shahzad A. Lipid Profile and Cardiovascular Risk Monitoring in Patients on Clozapine – an Audit at a Community Mental Health Resource Centre in Scotland. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S260-S261. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.628.

audits.title: Clozapine Monitoring in Older Adults: An Audit Evaluating Compliance With Clozapine Guidelines in Community Settings
audits.standard: Trust guideline: FBC, glucose, prolactin, U&E, lipids and LFTs every 6 months; HbA1c and clozapine plasma assay annually
audits.setting: Four Older Adult Community Mental Health Teams, Herefordshire and Worcestershire Health and Care NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Full compliance: FBC 100%; HbA1c 100%; LFTs 71%; U&E 57%; clozapine level 43%; glucose 0%; prolactin 0%; lipids 0% (43% had at least one test).

audits.other_findings: Many tests were done by GPs or hospitals for other reasons (e.g. 50% of U&Es, 71% of LFTs); authors suggest considering dedicated clozapine clinics.
audits.citation: Tong G, McCarthy M. Clozapine Monitoring in Older Adults: An Audit Evaluating Compliance With Clozapine Guidelines in Community Settings. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S266-S267. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.640.

audits.title: Improving Clozapine Blood Monitoring in Inpatient Psychiatry: A Targeted Quality Improvement Initiative
audits.standard: Trust guidelines: routine FBCs for all patients on clozapine and clozapine levels only on consultant guidance; target inappropriate tests reduced from 53% to zero by April 2024

cycle1.result: 53% of clozapine-related tests inappropriate, with missed FBCs.

audits.intervention: 20-minute training sessions for nurses on clozapine blood monitoring on three days, plus an aide-memoire at key ward locations.

cycle2.result: FBCs sent routinely for all patients on clozapine; no inappropriate clozapine level requests.

audits.other_findings: Staff confidence in clozapine monitoring increased on pre- and post-training questionnaires. Periodic refresher training was recommended.
audits.citation: Raja S, Lakda A. Improving Clozapine Blood Monitoring in Inpatient Psychiatry: A Targeted Quality Improvement Initiative. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S161-S161. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10429.

audits.title: A Clinical Audit on Pre-Treatment Assessment Protocol Adherence to Clozapine Therapy
audits.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines in Psychiatry, 13th edition, pre-clozapine assessment
audits.setting: Psychiatry units, Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore

cycle1.result: FBC, LFT, U&E and glucose 100%; ECG 76%; lipids 33%; ESR 19%; troponin 14%; CRP, BNP and physical examination 0%

audits.other_findings: Barriers included staff training, prescriber inconsistency and funding and staffing limits.

audits.title: Myocarditis monitoring during clozapine initiation: audit of practice in an NHS trust
audits.standard: Cardiac monitoring during clozapine initiation: baseline ECG and weekly troponin and CRP in the first 4 weeks (no standardised framework stated)
audits.setting: Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust; patients starting clozapine

cycle1.result: Of 219 patients, 180 had complete data. Baseline ECG completed in 80%. No routine troponin monitoring identified; CRP testing infrequent.

audits.other_findings: Tachycardia occurred in more than 40%; 15 referred to cardiology before initiation, 6 in the first 4 weeks and 5 thereafter; 12 (7%) discontinued clozapine early, mainly owing to tachycardia. Authors propose adding weekly troponin and CRP to mandatory blood tests.
audits.citation: Bridges M, Secchi A, Kumar Y, Nettey V, Bahia J, Whiskey E, et al.. Myocarditis monitoring during clozapine initiation: audit of practice in an NHS trust. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(5). doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.12079.
